events.title: William of Normandy defeats Harold II at Hastings
events.description: After a day-long battle near Hastings, Norman forces killed King Harold II and broke the English army. The conquest replaced England's ruling class and transformed its language, law and architecture.
events.html: After a day-long battle near Hastings, Norman forces killed King Harold II and broke the English army. The conquest replaced England's ruling class and transformed its language, law and architecture.

events.title: Robert the Bruce routs Edward II at Old Byland
events.description: A Scottish army under Robert the Bruce defeated English forces at Old Byland in Yorkshire, and Edward II narrowly escaped capture. The defeat pushed England towards the truce of 1323.
events.html: A Scottish army under Robert the Bruce defeated English forces at Old Byland in Yorkshire, and Edward II narrowly escaped capture. The defeat pushed England towards the truce of 1323.

events.title: King Tabinshwehti of Burma begins his invasion of Siam
events.description: A Toungoo force of 12,000 led by Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung invaded Siam through the Three Pagodas Pass and advanced to Ayutthaya. It failed to take the fortified capital, and Siamese counterattacks broke the siege in January 1549.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, goes on trial at Fotheringhay
events.description: Mary was tried before a commission of English peers and officials at Fotheringhay Castle, accused of plotting Elizabeth I's death in the Babington Plot. Found guilty, she was beheaded in February 1587.

events.title: An Austrian army surprises Frederick the Great at Hochkirch
events.description: In the Third Silesian War, an Austrian army of 80,000 under Leopold Josef Graf Daun surprised Frederick the Great's Prussian army of 30,000–36,000 at Hochkirch, near Bautzen in Saxony, and forced a general retreat. It was a rare defeat for Frederick.

events.title: Dwight D. Eisenhower is born in Texas
events.description: Dwight David Eisenhower was born in Denison, Texas. He commanded the Allied invasion of Europe in 1944 and served two terms as the 34th US president, warning on leaving office of the 'military-industrial complex'.

events.title: Chuck Yeager flies faster than sound
events.description: Captain Chuck Yeager piloted the rocket-powered Bell X-1 past Mach 1 high over the Mojave Desert. It was the first confirmed supersonic flight in level flight, opening the age of supersonic aviation.
events.html: Captain Chuck Yeager piloted the rocket-powered Bell X-1 past Mach 1 high over the Mojave Desert. It was the first confirmed supersonic flight in level flight, opening the age of supersonic aviation.

events.title: Soviet leaders oust Nikita Khrushchev
events.description: Recalled from holiday, Nikita Khrushchev was forced out by the Communist Party's Central Committee. Leonid Brezhnev succeeded him as party leader and steered the Soviet Union into two decades of stability and stagnation.
